outcome: Neonatal intensive care unit admission rate
cohort: 141 singleton pregnancies conceived by IVF and 141 singleton pregnancies conceived naturally, matched by maternal age
finding: Singleton pregnancies after IVF were not associated with higher risks of adverse obstetric and perinatal outcomes compared to naturally conceived pregnancies, but IVF pregnancies are associated with a higher rate of cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was significantly more common among women in the IVF group (74.4% vs. 54.6%, p<0.001), and the majority were elective cases (61.9% vs. 23.4%, p<0.001).
gest_age: IVF group: 37.9 ± 2.0 weeks; naturally conceived group: 38.4 ± 1.6 weeks
